items.stem: In Business Central, what does Assisted Setup help you do?

options.text: Guide configuration of scenarios and add features during implementation
options.rationale: Correct: assisted setup guides configure scenarios such as company creation and feature enablement.

options.text: Permanently lock the chart of accounts
options.rationale: Assisted setup configures; it does not lock the chart of accounts.
Assisted setup does not manage or replace extensions.
Posted entries cannot be deleted through assisted setup.

items.stem: Which TWO documents are part of the Business Central sales process? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: quotes are a standard sales document that can convert to an order.
Correct: sales orders record and post sales, including drop shipments.
Bank reconciliation is a cash-management task, not a sales document.
Routings belong to manufacturing, not sales.

items.stem: Why should business logic be added through extensions rather than changing base objects?

options.text: Extensions keep customisations upgrade-safe and separate from the base application
options.rationale: Correct: extensions isolate custom code so updates to Business Central do not overwrite it.

options.text: Extensions run faster than all base code
options.rationale: Performance is not the reason; upgrade safety and isolation are.

options.text: Base objects cannot be read by users
options.rationale: Base objects are readable; the issue is maintainability on upgrade.

options.text: Extensions remove the need for permissions
options.rationale: Permissions still apply to extended functionality.

items.explanation: Correct: extensions isolate custom code so updates to Business Central do not overwrite it.
